newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ denies slow bank loans behind sluggish M2+CD.
newsitem.headline: BOJ denies slow bank loans behind sluggish M2+CD.

text.p: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) denied on Thursday that slow lending by banks was behind the sluggish 2.7 percent growth in money supply in March, the lowest in 17 months.
"Banks' stance in making loans (to companies) is not a factor behind the fall in money supply, given that their loan growth was not declining significantly," a BOJ official told a news conference.

His statement was in response to a question on whether Japanese banks' struggle to write off bad loans had made them cautious about making fresh loans to companies, thus contributing to the slow money supply growth.

Earlier, the BOJ said that Japan's broadly defined money supply average of M2 plus certificates of deposit (CDs) grew a preliminary 2.7 percent in March from a year earlier. It grew a revised three percent year-on-year in February.
The 2.7 percent growth was the slowest since October 1995, when it also grew by 2.7 percent.
"We do not have to come to the conclusion that a change is taking place in the real economy using only a single month's data (on the money supply)," the official said.
The BOJ official said that despite the fall in M2 plus CD money supply growth throughout the January-March quarter, the broadest money measure had been steady.
Liquidity shifted around in the broadest money measure, he added.

The broadest money measure includes postal savings deposits at argicultural financial institutions and trust banks, bank debentures, Japanese government bonds, investment trusts and foreign bonds, along with M2 plus CDs.
The broadest money measure grew a preliminary 3.6 percent in March on a year-on-year basis, compared with 3.8 percent in February.

Yasunari Ueno, chief market economist at Fuji Securities Co Ltd's research group, said: "The slow money growth (for March) was partly due to a 'credit crunch' caused by banks' reluctance to lend money and due to a drop in large-lot deposits at banks."
Meanwhile, individual investors' buying of foreign bonds added to the steady growth in the broader liquidity measure for March, he said.
Banks were refraining from taking large-lot deposits, particularly in March, he said, as an increase would have required them to make larger contributions to Japan's deposit-insurance system.
